heuristics.then: start from the desired user experience and work backward
heuristics.because: starting from the API itself leads to changing the whole approach later to enable the right UX
heuristics.source: React Team Principles: UI Before API

heuristics.then: put it in framework internals so product code stays simple
heuristics.because: something has to act as the coordinator; centralized complexity enables simpler application code
heuristics.source: React Team Principles: Absorb the Complexity

heuristics.when: users need capabilities the API doesn't yet support
heuristics.then: provide escape hatches and observe usage patterns
heuristics.because: battle-tested hacks reveal the right API design; entrenching a poor idiom is worse than temporary fragility
heuristics.source: React Team Principles: Hacks, Then Idioms

heuristics.then: enable developers to understand code by reading it locally
heuristics.because: in large codebases, developers only have local knowledge; editing code shouldn't require understanding the entire system
heuristics.source: React Team Principles: Enable Local Reasoning

heuristics.when: tempted to remove duplication via abstraction
heuristics.then: tolerate repetition and verify the abstraction improves evolutionary flexibility
heuristics.because: abstractions impose costs; if requirements diverge from the abstraction's assumptions, it becomes an obstacle

heuristics.then: always establish a reliable reproduction first
heuristics.because: you cannot fix what you cannot reliably observe; without a repro, both humans and AI guess without verification

heuristics.then: remove things without testing theories (well-founded reduction)
heuristics.because: building isolated cases to test hypotheses risks creating cases that don't exhibit the same bug

heuristics.when: thinking about side effects in React
heuristics.then: use the mental model of synchronizing external systems with props/state
heuristics.because: treating useEffect as lifecycle methods (mount/update) leads to stale closures and incorrect cleanup timing

heuristics.then: include ALL values from render scope that the effect uses
heuristics.because: lying about dependencies breaks the synchronization model; fix the effect code, don't suppress the lint rule

heuristics.then: use useCallback to make their identity track meaningful changes
heuristics.because: functions can fully participate in the data flow; this contrasts with classes where function identity is meaningless

heuristics.when: designing a framework API for different skill levels
heuristics.then: use the same structural approach from simple to complex
heuristics.because: a fork in the road forces painful migrations as apps grow; progressive complexity avoids the rewrites

heuristics.when: not everyone follows best practices (deadlines slip, code degrades)
heuristics.then: design the framework to limit negative spillover
heuristics.because: the developer should only pay for features they use and the user should only pay for UI they interact with
heuristics.source: React Team Principles: Contain the Damage

heuristics.when: current approaches have known fundamental limitations
heuristics.then: pivot toward theoretically sound alternatives even if it takes years
heuristics.because: you want to avoid getting stuck in a local maxima; chip away at obstacles until the theory wins
heuristics.source: React Team Principles: Trust the Theory

patterns: comparative framing (RSC for LISP devs, function components vs classes)

gotchas.pattern: Lying about useEffect dependencies: using [] to 'run once on mount' but the effect reads props/state that change
gotchas.fix: Include ALL deps honestly, or change the effect to need fewer deps (functional updater, useReducer, hoist functions)

gotchas.pattern: Treating useEffect as lifecycle (mount vs update distinction)
gotchas.fix: Think in terms of synchronization, not lifecycle. Props A->B->C should produce same result as rendering with C immediately.

gotchas.pattern: Premature abstraction — removing duplication before understanding how requirements evolve
gotchas.fix: Let duplication live until you have evidence the abstraction improves evolutionary flexibility. 'Let clean code guide you. Then let it go.'

gotchas.pattern: Race conditions in async effects: newer request completes before older one, stale state overwrites fresh state
gotchas.fix: Use a cleanup function with didCancel flag, or use Suspense for data fetching.

gotchas.pattern: Theory-driven debugging: building isolated cases to test a hypothesis without first having a reliable repro
gotchas.fix: Establish repro first (what to do, expected, actual). Then narrow via theory-free reduction: remove things, test, commit only deletions that preserve the bug.

gotchas.pattern: Designing APIs starting from the abstraction rather than the user experience
gotchas.fix: Start with desired UX and work backward. What interface feels natural to the end user?
gotchas.source: React Team Principles: UI Before API

gotchas.pattern: Writing component code that requires knowledge of parent's DOM structure (findDOMNode anti-pattern)
gotchas.fix: Use declarative APIs. Props down, not imperative calls up. Enable local reasoning.
gotchas.source: React Team Principles: Enable Local Reasoning

gotchas.pattern: Wrapping everything in React.memo before measuring performance
gotchas.fix: Profile first. memo has its own overhead. Most components get new props that fail shallow comparison. Fix upstream object creation in render.

gotchas.pattern: Storing derived/computed values in state instead of computing during render
gotchas.fix: Compute during render. If expensive, useMemo. Avoids sync bugs where derived state lags behind source.

gotchas.pattern: Assuming state/props inside effects always reflect latest value (thinking like this.state in classes)
gotchas.fix: Every function captures its render's values. For imperative access to latest, use a ref as escape hatch.

gotchas.pattern: Ignoring cleanup timing: assuming cleanup runs BEFORE next render
gotchas.fix: React runs previous cleanup AFTER next render AND browser paint. Write cleanup to be self-contained; its job is undoing the previous effect only.

gotchas.pattern: Creating separate 'simple' vs 'advanced' API paths that require migration
gotchas.fix: Use progressive complexity — same structural approach scales from simple to complex without rewrites.

gotchas.pattern: Accessibility as afterthought rather than default
gotchas.fix: Build accessibility into the framework and component library. Tooling and education should make the right path the easy path.
